Executive Order 13261 of March 19, 2002 (67 FR 13243), section 4(d), replaced section 3(a) of Executive Order 13244. Before: the held 2001 text of section 3(a) says that no individual serving in an office listed in section 2(a)-(f) in an acting capacity shall act as Secretary pursuant to this Executive Order. After: the replacement text keeps the same offices, section 2(a)-(f), and the same bar but adds the words that no such individual shall act as Secretary by virtue of so serving, and refers to this order instead of this Executive Order. Under the strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, and the amendment is a later event with its own date; the substance changed in a limited way (it clarifies that the bar applies to service by virtue of the acting office). The 13261 amendment is on signing (March 19, 2002; Federal Register issue of March 21, 2002). Section 4 revokes Executive Order 11487 of October 6, 1969. A revocation is complete when made and nothing in the order defers it, so this clause was performed on signing, December 18, 2001 (the order was filed December 20, 2001 and published December 21, 2001, 66 FR 66267). The first end is therefore performance on issue, earlier than the revocation of the whole order in 2020; the order's own end (April 14, 2020) is the latest first end among the clauses and is the whole-order end.

research_rationale:
EO 13244 (Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of the Interior; 66 FR 66267, December 21, 2001) was read in full from the held Federal Register original. It sets a standing order of succession for the Secretary of the Interior. It was amended once (EO 13261, March 19, 2002, section 3(a) only) and was expressly revoked in its entirety by section 4 of EO 13915 (April 14, 2020; 85 FR 21733), whose text is held; EO 13915 then re-issues a similar succession order of its own. No held source shows an earlier end. The catalog note (Revokes: EO 11487; Amended by: EO 13261; Revoked by: EO 13915), the held 5 U.S.C. 3345 note and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register catalog and saved order texts) agree. The status decision records 'no': the order was formally revoked and has no operative force on 2026-10-14.
